title: A complete linear system containing a closed-immersion subsystem is closed
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $V\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-subspace whose associated morphism $j:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M$. Then the morphism associated to the complete linear system $\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ is a closed immersion and pulls back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $\mathcal M$.

source.place: no Stacks tag states it; standard linear-projection argument: the projection from P(Gamma(X,M)^vee) to P(V^vee) is defined where the coordinates in V do not all vanish, cancellation of closed immersions along a separated morphism (Schemes 07RK (3) (Morphisms, closed-immersion cancellation; the earlier 01KT is the section-immersion lemma, corrected by L, reviewer R-cls)), and Morphisms Lemma 01W6 (a proper immersion has closed image)

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, the unique morphism to the empty projective space of its zero space of sections is a closed immersion, and the pullback assertion is vacuous. Otherwise, properness over the field implies $X$ is of finite type over the Noetherian $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence locally Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The invertible $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module], so it is of finite type; it is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Thus $W:=\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] with $i=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XZ (coherent iff quasi-coherent of finite type on a locally Noetherian scheme), and Lemma 02O6 (finite coherent cohomology over a Noetherian affine base)

proof.text: Choose a basis $s_0,\ldots,s_r$ of $V$ and extend it to a basis $s_0,\ldots,s_N$ of $W$; both are finite by step 1. Since $j$ is the morphism associated with $V$, its defining sections generate $\mathcal M$ at every point by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points]. Consequently the extended family also generates $\mathcal M$. The same node gives the morphism $\phi:X\to\mathbf P(W^\vee)_k$ of the complete system, with $\phi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M$ carrying the coordinate sections to $s_i$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NE (lemma-projective-space), generating sections and their associated morphism

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq\mathbf P(W^\vee)_k$ be the union of the standard opens $D_+(T_0),\ldots,D_+(T_r)$ corresponding to the basis of $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] these are exactly the nonvanishing loci of those coordinate sections. The sections $T_0,\ldots,T_r$ therefore generate $\mathcal O(1)|_U$, and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] defines a $k$-morphism $p:U\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)_k$. Since $s_0,\ldots,s_r$ generate $\mathcal M$, $\phi(X)\subseteq U$. Pulling the $T_i$ back through $p\circ\phi$ gives $s_i$, so uniqueness in the functor-of-points statement gives $p\circ\phi=j$ (with $\phi$ regarded as a map to $U$).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NE (lemma-projective-space) and Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); projection defined only on the union of the indicated standard opens

proof.text: The projective space $\mathbf P(W^\vee)_k$ is separated over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Hence its open subscheme $U$ is separated over $k$: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of projective space to $U\times_kU$. Since $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and factors through $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] (b) makes $p$ separated. Now $p\circ\phi=j$ is a closed immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-cancellation] makes $X\to U$ a closed immersion. Composing with the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(W^\vee)_k$ makes $\phi$ an immersion. Also $X$ is proper over $k$ and $\mathbf P(W^\vee)_k$ is separated over $k$, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $\phi$ proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed], $\phi$ is a closed immersion. Its pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ is $\mathcal M$ by step 2.

lean.statement: theorem completeLinearSystem_isClosedImmersion (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : letI : Module k Γ(M, ⊤) := Module.compHom Γ(M, ⊤) (Scheme.globalSectionsRingHom k (X := X)) ∀ (I : Type u) [Finite I] (s : I → M.sections) (hs : Epi (M.freeHomEquiv.symm s)), LinearIndependent (M := Γ(M, ⊤)) k (fun i ↦ (s i).val (Opposite.op ⊤)) → IsClosedImmersion (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) M s hs) → Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) M s hs)).obj (ProjectiveSpace.twist I (Spec (.of k)) 1) ≅ M) → ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : Finite J) (t : J → M.sections) (ht : Epi (M.freeHomEquiv.symm t)), LinearIndependent (M := Γ(M, ⊤)) k (fun j ↦ (t j).val (Opposite.op ⊤)) ∧ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun j ↦ (t j).val (Opposite.op ⊤) : Set Γ(M, ⊤)) = ⊤ ∧ IsClosedImmersion (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections J (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) M t ht) ∧ Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections J (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) M t ht)).obj (ProjectiveSpace.twist J (Spec (.of k)) 1) ≅ M)
